proof_attempt_summary: Derived and independently reviewed a fully charged finite hybrid protocol and matching shared-source matrix converse for every fixed rho>0. The leading normalized pilot cost is rho(2-3rho)/(6(1-rho)) for 0<rho<2/3 and zero for rho>=2/3; the boundary claims only zero leading cost. All math and cited-source checks pass, but the field floor is unmet (subfield, ceiling7.1<7.4, not salvageable); no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: For one randomized source study and \(K=\lfloor\rho d_N\rfloor\) independent covariate-only targets, we determine the sharp leading total pilot cost at maximum marginal mean squared error \(C_0/N\) and common broadcast allowance \(K\{\lceil(\log_2N)/2\rceil+b_0\}\). For every fixed \(\rho>0\), the coefficient is \(\rho(2-3\rho)/\{6(1-\rho)\}\) below \(2/3\), and zero from \(2/3\) onward. A fully charged finite occupancy-adaptive code attains the coefficient, and a posterior matrix decision bound proves the converse while retaining unknown sampled masses, parallel pilots and terminal raw covariate data.
gap: The completed scalar predecessor determines one short-reply threshold. The checked distributed-expectation and Gaussian-vector results do not identify the leading pilot cost when independent target queries share one source response.
fill: The proposed matrix posterior inequality retains a small public subset of pilot lengths and restores the other independent query rows. A charged occupancy-based cell release and residual-answer code provide the constructive handle for determining the sharp crossover.
